listing.name: Crash Team Racing / CTR Native
listing.summary: Explore Crash Team Racing / CTR Native and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Use your own USA raw disc
steps.instruction: For an existing official beta7.1 Windows copy, choose ctr_native.exe inside its extracted wrapper, with that executable’s folder as the working directory. Place your own NTSC-U raw MODE2/2352 disc BIN at assets/ctr-u.bin beside it; the data track must start at byte 0. A cooked 2048 ISO, another edition or a CUE file is not this route. No compiler, BIOS or extraction helper is needed for the official player archive. Windows runs its x86 player through x64 compatibility; upstream also offers a separate 32-bit Linux package with its own dependency requirements.

steps.title: Prefer in-game memory-card saves
steps.instruction: Normal saves and ghosts live under memcards. F12 captures SCREENSHOT.BMP and the VRAM debug capture uses VRAM.TGA. Internal F5 quickstates under debug/states hold runtime memory and are tied to their creating build; replay reports under debug/reports can include independent recorded memory-card progress. Keep the old runtime with those files for matching-build use; do not insert them into another version.

steps.title: Keep external ownership or preserve debug output before retrying
steps.instruction: You or upstream update an external copy. Keep its complete working folder and back up memcards and captures before extracting a new player separately. Keep debug output with the originating runtime for matching-build use; no cross-version state compatibility is promised. External registration preserves every file and supplies no managed Backup or Rollback.

source_requirements.label: Your USA retail raw Crash Team Racing BIN

presentation.manual_preparation: Portcove copies your verified USA raw disc into the official player; no installer or compiler is required. Compatible updates preserve the verified disc copy, in-game memory-card saves, ghosts and captures. Backups include the original disc and can be large; keep them private. Prefer in-game saves: internal F5 quickstates and replay reports belong to their creating runtime. If debug output holds Play or an update after exit, preserve/move the exact shown files outside the managed folder and retain their original runtime before retrying. They are never inserted into a successor. Runtime rollback keeps current declared saves and does not guarantee older software can read them. The Windows x86 player runs on x64 Windows; OpenGL 3.3 is required.
